name: Tribal Guardian (Unchained Barbarian)
body:
Not all barbarians go out and raid or crush their foes, some are tasked with protecting the clan hold. These are tribal guardians.

Valorous Deflection (Ex)

At 1st level, when an opponent makes a melee attack against the tribal guardian or an adjacent ally, if they are raging, they can expend a round of their rage and a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry the attack. They make an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity. For each size category the attacking creature is larger, the tribal guardian takes a -2 penalty to this attack. If the attempt is made using a shield attack, the tribal guardian may apply any enhancement or ability bonuses to shield AC to the attack. If the attack result is greater than the attackers, the attack automatically misses. The attempt must be declared before the results of the attack are known.

If this attack is made while they are using the Combat Expertise feat, fighting defensively, or taking the total defense action they may also add the bonus from those abilities to the attack roll to block an attack, but loses any used bonuses until the beginning of their next turn.

Upon a successful parry, if the tribal guardian still has remaining rounds of rage, they may make a riposte attack on the creature they parried as an immediate action, provided the target is in their threatened area. If the parry attempt fails, the attack is instead directed at the tribal guardian at its normal result and the guardian is flat-footed and loses their shield bonus to AC if the shield was used in the attempt.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 2nd level.

Behind Me (Ex)

At 2nd level, the tribal protector may elect to place themselves in the path of danger in order to protect an ally. When rolling initiative, the tribal protector may select a target as a charge. This selection may not change for the duration of the encounter. Any time that they are within 5 feet of their charge, and the charge is the target of an attack, the tribal guardian may, as an immediate action, enter the square occupied by the charge and receive the attack in their place. The attack automatically hits the tribal guardian. The charge is placed in any empty square adjacent to the tribal guardian of their choice. They may activate this ability after knowing whether their charge will be hit.

If the tribal guardian suffers a critical hit as a result of using behind me they regain a round of rage.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 4th level.

Ever Vigilant (Ex)

At 6th level, while raging, all squares the tribal guardian threatens with a melee weapon or unarmed strike, are considered difficult terrain for enemies. This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the tribal guardian wields a melee weapon or unarmed strike capable of affecting them. The tribal guardian must be aware of the enemy to affect them.

The tribal guardian also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if their square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 6th level.

Stalwart (Ex)

At 8th level, while raging, if the tribal guardian succeeds at a Fortitude or Will save against an effect that would have a partial effect on a successful save they instead suffer no effects.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 8th level.

Death Before Dishonor (Ex)

At 10th level, the tribal guardian gains Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. At any time while the Diehard feat is active and the tribal guardian is raging, they suppress the staggered condition for the round.

Any strenuous action still causes damage as normal.

Additionally, if the tribal guardian’s hit points are below their Constitution score, they may expend an additional round of rage each round to continue to act under the Diehard feat until they reach a negative hp total equal to their tribal guardian class levels plus their Constitution score. During this time, they still suppress the staggered condition while raging.

If the tribal guardian ends their rage while still within this threshold, they are considered dying and stable for one round. If they do not receive healing within the round to bring their hit points back above their Constitution score, they die.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 10th level.

Bring ‘em Down (Ex)

At 12th level, the tribal guardian is able to defend their immediate area against all who would attempt to force their way by. As long as the tribal guardian is raging they may make attacks of opportunity against foes that enter their threatened area even if under the effect of a spell or ability that otherwise prevents attacks of opportunity such as Flyby Attack or Improved Grapple. If this attack hits, the tribal guardian may expend an additional round of their rage to deal damage as normal and if the attack roll would also beat the target’s CMD, they are tripped.

This ability allows the tribal guardian to trip flying creatures. A flying creature tripped by this ability falls to the ground.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 12th level.

Implacable (Ex)

At 14th level, while raging, the tribal guardian is no longer slowed by difficult terrain, whether natural, magical, or magically augmented.

Additionally, the tribal guardian is not slowed by effects which reduce their base move speed, and become immune to the dazed and stunned conditions so long as they remain conscious.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 14th level.

Overwhelming Presence (Ex)

At 16th level, as a swift action usable once per rage, the tribal guardian may project their superior skill and strength of arms to all enemies, weeding out the weak and allowing only the strong to face them. All enemies within 60 feet of the tribal guardian must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 their class levels + their Strength modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat. Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more or has fewer HD than the tribal guardian’s character level minus 4 is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken as long as they can see and hear the tribal guardian. Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 16th level.

Incredible Recovery (Ex)

At 18th level, the tribal guardian’s ability to recover from injury is truly extraordinary. They gain fast healing 1 when not in combat. This cannot restore hit points lost to starvation, thirst, or suffocation nor does it reattach severed limbs.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 18th level.

Unstoppable (Ex)

At 18th level, while the tribal guardian is raging and is conscious they are immune to the entangled, grappled, pinned, petrified, and paralyzed conditions.

This ability replaces the rage power given at 20th level.
